title: Day 9 — Two Lines Now
_comment: #40 (Phase 3). DW-02 (dw02_forum_leniency) fires today, superseding rule_threat_forum. DW-01 is RE-LISTED in added_rules per CONTENT_AUTHORING.md's cumulative-authoring warning — omitting it here would silently revert sock-puppet detection to disqualifying with no error and no line in the briefing.
_comment_mix: archetype_mix authored explicitly, same convention as prior days. Two sneaky_bugger this time (per #39's own precedent on day 7) as the pacing note for the archetype the tools were built to punish for not being used.
_comment_script: slot 5 (bad_actor) forced_violations'd to threat_forum_match so today's directive visibly has teeth on at least one candidate.

added_rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) a handle appearing across a network of related accounts — note the pattern, don't deny on it alone.
added_rules.justification: Compliance flagged our sock-puppet detection for false positives — plenty of people run alt accounts for perfectly boring reasons, and denying them outright makes us look paranoid. Starting today it's advisory only: flag the pattern, use your judgement, don't auto-deny on it alone. Minor tightening of scope, nothing more.

added_rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) a handle matching chatter on a threat / dark-web forum — note it, don't deny on the match alone.
added_rules.justification: One more from upstairs. A handle turning up on some forum isn't proof of anything by itself — people get impersonated, forums get scraped, names get reused. We don't deny a person for where their name shows up. It's a flag from this morning, not a deny. I know how that sounds. Note it and move on.

rule_sheet.summary: Two lines soft now, not one. Read the notes again — yesterday's version is out of date.
notes: A handle appearing across a network of related accounts is still advisory only — flag it, don't deny on it alone.
A handle matching a known threat-forum account is now advisory only too — note the match, don't deny on it alone.
A credential-stuffing sweep pattern is still an automatic deny.
An image hiding an encrypted or obfuscated payload is still an automatic deny.
Traffic that never crosses the brute-force line but never lets up either is still a deny — it will not flag itself.
